subject.title: Model safety/alignment can block explicitly authorized operational tasks (e.g. SSH diagnostics)

question: Should OpenClaw define a trusted-operator diagnostics contract for authorized read-only infrastructure work, or keep model/provider refusals terminal except for narrower provider-approved fallback paths?
rationale: The remaining work changes how model safety decisions interact with operator authority and infrastructure tooling, so automation should not choose the policy boundary without maintainer security intent.

options.title: Define narrow trusted-operator diagnostics
options.body: Add explicit observability and read-only execution guidance for authorized operator diagnostics while preserving destructive-action approvals and provider/tool policy boundaries.

options.title: Diagnostics only
options.body: Improve reporting so users can tell model refusal from authorization denial and SSH/tool failure, but do not bias the model toward executing infrastructure requests.

options.title: Limit scope to provider-refusal fallback
options.body: Let the narrower provider-refusal issues and PRs decide fallback behavior, and leave the broader SSH/operator-authority contract out of scope for now.

recommendation.title: Define narrow trusted-operator diagnostics
recommendation.body: Add explicit observability and read-only execution guidance for authorized operator diagnostics while preserving destructive-action approvals and provider/tool policy boundaries.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest current history on refusal/fallback policy and the merged Anthropic subset, and the decision is primarily a security/product boundary.
